title: A Current for the Summit
premise: Ada Okonkwo, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vane Syndicate's cheerful enforcers, is paid in a dying prospector's map: coordinates to a wrecked salvage ship holding a fortune in unclaimed cargo. Racing six tides against the Syndicate's own fleet—and trailed by Idris, a Syndicate defector whose loyalties Ada cannot trust and cannot resist—Ada must decide whether the wreck's true prize is wealth or proof of the Syndicate's crimes. At the climax, Ada reaches the wreck on the final tide, chooses to sink the evidence rather than sell it, and exposes the Syndicate anyway through Idris's testimony. In the end, Ada loses the fortune but gains a name worth keeping, and a partner for the next storm.
about_author: C. M. Crane is the pen name of a former marine surveyor who spent a decade charting coastlines from Nova Scotia to the Coral Sea before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people who make bad bargains with beautiful, indifferent places.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector Smiles
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A storm-chasing run goes wrong when the Vane Syndicate's amiable enforcer, Mr. Pell, collects on Ada's debt with a deadline and a threat wrapped in courtesy. The chapter establishes Ada's skill, isolation, and desperation. Emotional beat: dread disguised as charm.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Tide Line
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. On a supply run, Ada finds a prospector named Ede collapsed on the flats, gut-shot and dying. He offers a map to the wreck of the Meridian Star in exchange for one promise: deliver it to his daughter, not to any fleet. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Reading the map, Ada realizes the wreck sits in a tidal basin accessible only at low water—six tides remain before the season closes it. The Syndicate's salvage fleet is already provisioning nearby. Ada decides to run. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Man Who Jumped Ship
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Introduced as a Syndicate navigator who defects mid-voyage after glimpsing what the fleet truly hunts—not just cargo but documents. He intercepts Ada, offering his knowledge of the fleet's route. Emotional beat: calculated risk wearing the mask of sincerity.

chapters.title: Terms of Passage
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada interrogates Idris over a fire, unable to verify a word he says but needing his charts. They strike an uneasy bargain: he navigates, she keeps him alive until the wreck. Emotional beat: wary attraction kindling under mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: Through the Squeeze
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The pair races a rising storm through a narrow channel the Syndicate believes impassable. Idris's navigation saves them; Ada's boat-handling saves him. First real trust forms. Emotional beat: exhilaration—the first joy either has felt in years.

chapters.title: What Pell Knows
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Aboard the flagship Vane Fortune, Pell reports the defection and reveals the Syndicate's secret: the Meridian Star carried ledgers implicating half the coastal governments. His superiors order no witnesses. Emotional beat: cold ambition masking unease.

chapters.title: Ede's Daughter
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A detour to deliver the map's promise leads Ada to Nara, Ede's estranged daughter, who refuses forgiveness and demands answers about her father's last years. Ada learns Ede was once Syndicate too. Emotional beat: guilt deepening—Ada inherited more than a map.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Shadow
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Idris confesses partially: he didn't defect for conscience alone; the Syndicate killed his brother for reading those ledgers. Ada must weigh whether his vengeance will burn them both. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in shared damage.

chapters.title: Third Tide, False Harbor
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A seemingly safe anchorage turns out to be a Syndicate listening post. Ada and Idris barely escape, but the escape broadcasts their position. Pell now knows exactly where they are. Emotional beat: paranoia—the wilderness itself feels watched.

chapters.title: Nara's Choice
chapters.summary: Nara's POV. Nara, following her own clues from Ede's letters, catches up to Ada and forces herself aboard. She carries the second half of the map—a piece Ede never sent. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose; the promise becomes a partnership.

chapters.title: Storm Country
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. To lose the fleet, Ada does the unthinkable: sails directly into a named storm, using her chasing skills to ride its edge while the Syndicate ships scatter. The sequence showcases her mastery. Emotional beat: transcendence—Ada belongs to the storm more than to any debt.

chapters.title: After the Eye
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. In the storm's calm center, Ada and Idris finally speak plainly—about duty, identity, and who they might be if they survive. They become lovers. Emotional beat: tenderness inside catastrophe; love chosen against every practical instinct.

chapters.title: The Fleet Regroups
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. The storm cost the Syndicate two ships and their patience. Command authorizes lethal force and offers Pell a promotion contingent on results. Pell begins to suspect he is expendable too. Emotional beat: corruption devouring its own.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Fourth Tide
chapters.summary: Nara's POV. A Syndicate patrol corners them; someone signaled their position. Evidence points to Idris, and Nara demands Ada maroon him. Ada refuses, splitting the group's trust down the middle. Emotional beat: heartbreak—the cost of loving a man with secrets.

chapters.title: The Truth in the Bilge
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Idris proves his innocence: the signal came from a tracker sewn into Ede's map case, planted by the Syndicate long ago. Ede was bait all along. The revelation reframes everything. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by horror—they were never ahead, only permitted.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide: The Wreck Opens
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At extreme low water, the Meridian Star's hull emerges from the sand. Ada, Idris, and Nara breach the hold and find the ledgers intact—but so, waiting on the ridge above, does Pell's landing party. Emotional beat: triumph curdling instantly into siege.

chapters.title: Standoff in the Hold
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Trapped between collapsing tide walls and Pell's guns, Ada negotiates while Nara secretly copies ledger pages and Idris rigs the wreck's unstable fuel stores. Emotional beat: desperate clarity—every character choosing what they will die for.

chapters.title: The Sixth Tide
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The climax. Ada triggers the fuel collapse, destroying the wreck, the ledgers' originals, and nearly everyone—including herself—as the sea reclaims the basin. Pell drowns reaching for the very fortune that defined him. Emotional beat: sacrifice as identity—Ada becomes what she always was beneath the debt.

chapters.title: What the Sea Kept
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Idris drags Ada from the surf; she survives, broken but alive. Nara's copied pages survived in waterproof wrap. The three regroup on open water with almost nothing but the truth. Emotional beat: exhausted gratitude and the first honest hope.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Nara's POV. The copies reach a federal magistrate through channels Ede trusted decades ago. Arrests ripple up the coast; the Syndicate fractures. Nara buries her father's name clean at last. Emotional beat: justice arriving quietly, without fireworks—duty fulfilled on their own terms.

chapters.title: A Current for the Summit
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Debt-free and name-clear, Ada stands at the headland where Ede died, watching a storm build on the horizon. Idris asks where she'll chase next. She smiles: anywhere the current runs. Emotional beat: resolution—identity reclaimed, love chosen freely, the wilderness still forgiving nothing and forgetting less.
